indicator_definition: This indicator measures the proportion of the population that is unable to keep their home adequately warm, as a share of total population. It is one of the key indicators of energy poverty in Europe. Data are collected through the EU Statistics on Income and Living Conditions (EU-SILC).
rationale: Energy poverty affects health, well-being and quality of life, particularly for low-income households. Ensuring that all people can afford to heat their homes is a fundamental dimension of affordable and clean energy. Progress means a sustained reduction in the share of the population experiencing energy poverty.
methodology_characteristics: Data are collected through EU-SILC, which asks respondents whether they can afford to keep their home adequately warm. The indicator is expressed as a percentage of the total population. Data are collected annually and published by Eurostat.
indicator_name: Population unable to keep home adequately warm
